breakfast.name: Menemen (Turkish Scramble)
breakfast.description: Turkish scrambled eggs with tomatoes, peppers, and onions served with fresh bread
instructions: Heat olive oil in large pan
Sauté onion and pepper until soft
breakfast.fun_fact: Menemen is a Turkish breakfast staple eaten throughout the country, especially in Izmir

lunch.name: Doner Kebab
lunch.description: Turkish marinated meat cooked on vertical spit, sliced thin and served with sauce
instructions: Mix ground meat with onion, garlic, spices
Roast vertically over coals/in oven at 450°F for 40-45 minutes
Slice thin from outside as it cooks
Serve in pita with tomato, cucumber, yogurt sauce
lunch.fun_fact: Döner Kebab is one of the most popular foods worldwide and is sold throughout Europe

dinner.name: Turkish Eggplant Stew
dinner.description: Layered eggplant and meat stew with tomato sauce and béchamel
instructions: Brown meat with onion and garlic
Make béchamel: melt butter, whisk flour, add milk
Layer eggplant and meat sauce in baking dish
dinner.notes: Must rest after baking to hold shape
dinner.fun_fact: Turkish version of Moussaka predates the Greek version

snacks.name: Turkish Hummus
snacks.description: Smooth chickpea dip with tahini, garlic, and lemon
instructions: Combine chickpeas, tahini, garlic in food processor
Blend until smooth, adding water as needed
snacks.fun_fact: Hummus is consumed daily in Turkish culture and throughout the Levant
alternatives: Top with pine nuts and spiced meat

desserts.name: Baklava (Phyllo with Honey)
desserts.description: Crispy phyllo pastry layered with pistachios and soaked in honey syrup
instructions: Layer 4 phyllo sheets in 9x13 pan with butter between each
Bake at 350°F for 35-40 minutes until golden
While baking, heat honey, water, lemon juice, spices
Pour hot honey over hot baklava
desserts.notes: Must pour hot syrup on hot baklava
desserts.fun_fact: Baklava was perfected in Ottoman palace kitchens and remains a symbol of Turkish cuisine

nonAlcoholicDrinks.name: Turkish Coffee
nonAlcoholicDrinks.description: Strong, thick coffee made in special pot with finely ground beans
instructions: Fill cezve (Turkish coffee pot) to top with water for 1 serving
Just before boiling, pour into cup, reserving some foam
Serve in small cup with foam on top
nonAlcoholicDrinks.notes: Coffee beans must be finely ground
nonAlcoholicDrinks.fun_fact: Turkish Coffee is UNESCO-recognized intangible cultural heritage

alcoholicDrinks.name: Rakı (Anise Spirit)
alcoholicDrinks.description: Turkish anise-flavored spirit served ice-cold with water and meze
instructions: Pour water slowly - it turns milky (called 'lion's milk')
alcoholicDrinks.fun_fact: Rakı is called 'lion's milk' because of the white color when water is added
